translation:
_Gurjar khandmein pragate, Gnani Gorakhnath; Das Kabire jeevna, mastak dino hath._ ||129|| — Prabodh
(In the land of Gujarat appeared Gorakhnath as the Knower [Gnani]; Das Kabir gave him spiritual life, placing his hand upon his head.)

Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj says that in the region of Gujarat, Gorakhnath appeared as Gnaniji. Das Kabir placed his hand on his head, graced him, and bestowed devotion upon him — there is another couplet [sakhi] like this:

_Gujaratmein gnani bhaye, jaanat hai sab koy; Das Kabira aayke, darshan deena soy._
(Everyone knows that a knower [gnani] such as this appeared in Gujarat; Das Kabira came and gave him his darshan.)

Everyone knows the fact that a devotee like Gnaniji appeared in Gujarat. Das Kabirji came and gave him darshan, making him fulfilled. In his previous birth, Gnaniji had been Gorakhnath. He had wasted his life in yogic practice and attained eighty-four siddhis [supernatural powers], and out of the pride these gave him he went to defeat Kabir — sitting upon a trident, he asked Kabirji to debate him. Kabirji took one end of a ball of thread used for weaving cloth, kept it on the ground, threw the thread up into the sky, and, sitting on its far end, asked Gorakhnath to come and sit facing him. Seeing this, Gorakhnath admitted defeat, gave up the five emblems of the Gorakh sect [Gorakhpanthi], and begged devotion from Kabirji — this is recounted in the Gorakh-Kabir Dialogue.

_Topi kopi koobadi jholi jhanda haath, kripa bhai Kabirki; Paancho maatra sompi deenhi Gorakhnath._
(The cap, loincloth, crutch, satchel, and flag in hand — when Kabir's grace fell upon him, Gorakhnath surrendered all five of these emblems.)

When Kabir's grace fell upon Gorakh, he handed over to Kabirji the cap, loincloth, crutch [under-arm staff], satchel, and flag — all five emblems.

The account of how Kabir told Gorakh — who had squandered his life in yogic practice — that he would grant him devotion when he took his second birth, is found in a text called the Garbhavali.

Gorakh said:

_Suno swami garabh bandhana, kaise hansa hoy chhootana; Kaise mite jathar-ki traasa, so saheb kaho hum paasa._
(Listen, O Master: how may the soul [hansa] bound in the womb be freed, and how may the torment of the womb-fire be ended? Tell me this, O Lord.)

Gorakh said, "O Swami! Listen — how may the soul [jivatma] bound in the womb be freed, and how may the torment of the digestive fire [jatharagni] in the womb end? Tell me this, Master."

Sadguru Kabir said:

_Ab main tumkun bhed bataai, desh Murdharmein janamo jaai; Jesalmer Murdhar mojhara, Bhathi ke ghar lyo avatara. Gnani hoye jo naam tumhara, khoji guruko lev vichara; Fir aavo Gujarat mojhara, Kanam mandal seedh bhom bandhana. Jahan hoy tumaro asthana, in dehise tohe samujhaai; Tumharo panth bichal sab jaai, tumaro bhekh chale sansara. Main tumhare jivka karo ubara, tum to boond sadhna keenha; Bhag dekhi tum boho daraana, taate garabhvasmein aai. Tumharo panth gaman hi paai, Gorakh manmein aisi aai. Deh dharun Sindhmein jaai, chhatri ghar leu avatara; Jugat jugatse karu ubara._
(Now I tell you the secret: go and take birth in the land of Murdhar [Marwar]. In Jaisalmer, within Murdhar, take incarnation in the house of the Bhati [Rajput clan]. Your name shall be Gnani [the Knower]; seek out the guru Khojiji and take his teaching. Then come again to Gujarat, and dwell in the plain, level land of the Kanam region — that shall be your abode. Through this very body I shall make you understand. Your entire [Gorakh] path will waver and be led astray, and the practice [bhekh] you adopt there will spread through the world. I shall deliver your soul, but right now you are engaged in the practice of retaining the seed [celibate discipline], and you are greatly afraid at the sight of the female organ — that is why you must enter the womb. The thought came into Gorakh's mind to follow the path Kabirji had shown — that he would take a body by going to Sindh, taking incarnation in a Kshatriya house, and through various means bring about his own deliverance.)

— Sakhi —

_Kahe Gorakh sadguru suno, main leu avatar; Fir tum hamkun kaise milo, so guru kaho vichar. Kar jodi Gorakh kahe, sunho swami sujaan; Sharan tumhari mohi rakh ho, dyo apna nijgyan._
(Gorakh says: "Sadguru, listen — I shall take incarnation, but then tell me, by what reasoning, how will you meet me again?" Folding his hands, Gorakh says: "Listen, O all-knowing Master, keep me in your refuge and grant me your own true knowledge.")

Kabir's word — Kabir says:

_Khoji mootat hans oothe, tum hi haso apaar; Tab khoji man sanse pare, tumse boojh deedar. Khojika saansa mite, sahje hoy ubaar. Batak beejki maandmein, dekh bhaya man dheer; Jan Gnanika sanse mita, sadguru mile Kabir. Kahe Kabir suno Gorakha, maano vachan hamaar; Nizh gyan samjhaavahu, doosar janam tumhaar. So Jesalmer (vaahitare) janamiya, Bhathi kul rajput; Gurjar dhar (desh) paavan kiyo, so gnani gun avadhoot._
(Kabir says: "When Khojiji laughs while relieving himself, you too shall laugh without measure. Then Khojiji will fall into doubt — 'I laughed, but why did you laugh?' — and to find out why, he will come searching for you. Then I shall grant you darshan, and Khojiji's doubt will be resolved; thus your deliverance shall come about with ease. Seeing the fig-fruit swept along in the stream, his mind grew steady." "The devotee Gnani's doubt was resolved when he met the Sadguru Kabir." Kabir says: "Listen, Gorakh, heed my word — I shall explain true knowledge to you in your next birth. So [Gorakh] was born in Jaisalmer, in the Bhati Rajput clan, and sanctified the land of Gujarat — that knower, endowed with the qualities of a true renunciate [avadhoot].")

Sadguru Kabir said, "Now I shall show you the way: go and take birth in the land of Murdhar. Having arrived in Jaisalmer, within Murdhar, take incarnation in the house of a Bhati [Rajput]. Your name will be Gnani, and you shall receive the teaching of Guru Khojiji. Then come to Gujarat and dwell in the plain, level land of the Kanam region — wherever your dwelling shall be. And I, through this very body of Kabir, shall make you understand; your entire Gorakh path will be led astray and abandoned, and the practice of devotion [bhekh-achar] that you adopt there will spread through the world. I shall bring about the deliverance of your soul, but right now you are engaged in the practice of preserving the seed [celibate discipline] and are greatly afraid at the sight of the female organ, and so you shall now enter the womb [take birth]." The thought arose in Gorakh's mind that he should follow the path Kabirji had shown him, and that he should go to Sindh and take incarnation as a Kshatriya, and through various stratagems bring about his own deliverance.

Sakhi — Gorakh began to say, "Sadguru, listen: I shall indeed take incarnation, but then explain to me how you will meet me again." Folding his hands, Gorakh said, "O all-knowing Master, listen: keep me in your refuge, and teach me your own knowledge." Kabir's word — Kabir says, "When Khojiji laughs while urinating, you too will laugh uncontrollably. Then Khojiji will suspect: 'I laughed, but why did you laugh?' — tell me the reason for my laughter. As you search for this reason, you will come looking for me, and then I shall give you darshan, and the doubt Khojiji had raised will be resolved — thus your deliverance shall come about with ease." Seeing the fig-fruit of the banyan tree being carried away in the urine, Khojiji's mind was struck with wonder, and the question this raised for Gnaniji was resolved when he later met Sadguru Kabir — that as long as the seed remained attached to the tree it was safe, but once separated from the tree it is carried away in filth and urine. In the same way, as long as the soul remains attached to the feet of the Lord it stays safe, but turning away from God it keeps drifting in the filth and urine of the womb of this ocean of worldly existence [bhavsagar]. The seed contains the tree within it, and the tree contains the seed within it — in this way the world is contained within God, and God within the world; the two are interwoven. Kabir went on to say, "O Gorakh, heed what I say — I shall explain my own true knowledge to you in your second incarnation." Thus this Gorakh was born in the dwelling of Jaisalmer, in the Bhatiya Rajput clan, and this Knower, possessing the qualities of a true renunciate, sanctified the land of Gujarat. Dayaldas has written about Gnaniji:

_Dayaala aise sadguru Kabir hai, jine Gorakhku chetaaye; Jaaki doormat metke, bandhan diye chhodaaye._ ||13||
(Dayal[das says]: such is the merciful Sadguru Kabir, who awakened Gorakh; erasing his ill understanding, he freed him from bondage.)

Dayaldas says that such is the merciful Sadguru Kabirji, who awakened Gorakh, and having removed the evil intellect [durmat] that was in him, freed him from the bonds of worldly existence.

_Dayaala sadguru das Kabirji, jine Gorakhkun diyo gyan; Gorakh ko saanso mityo, tabahi laagyo nishchal dhyan._ ||14||
(Dayal[das]: Sadguru Das Kabirji is such that he gave knowledge to Gorakh; when Gorakh's doubt was dispelled, he then fixed himself in unwavering meditation.)

Dayal[das says] — Sadguru Das Kabirji is such that he gave teaching to Gorakh, and when he dispelled Gorakh's doubts, Gorakh then engaged in unwavering devotion.

_Dayaala tab Gorakh man vicharke, mudra dhari utaar; He samrath kripa karo, mohe utaaro paar._ ||15||
(Dayal[das]: then Gorakh, reflecting in his mind, removed the yogic emblems [mudras] he wore, and said, "O capable one, be gracious and carry me across.")

Dayal[das] — then Gorakh, reflecting in his mind, removed the emblematic postures [mudras] of the yogic path and said to Kabir, "O capable Kabirji, now be gracious to me and deliver me across the ocean of existence."

_Dayaala tab sadguru boliya, janam dharo avataar; Fer paachhe janam dharo, tab hi utaru paar._ ||16||
(Dayal[das]: then the Sadguru said, "Take incarnation [now]; when you take your next birth after this, then I shall carry you across.")

Dayal[das] — then Sadguru Kabir said, "You must take a[nother] incarnation, and it is when you take that [next] birth that I shall carry you across."

_Dayaala Gorakh man vicharke, chaalyo Murdhar desh; Jesalmermein upanyo, naam dharyo naresh._ ||17||
(Dayal[das]: Gorakh, reflecting in his mind, set out for the land of Murdhar; he was born in Jaisalmer and was known there as a prince [naresh].)

Dayal[das] — Gorakh reflected and set out toward the land of Murdhar, and appeared [was born] in Jaisalmer, where he became known as a prince.

_Dayaala agiyaar varaski umare, tiko rajko hoy; Tab chatursinghe vichariyo, fand paduugo soy._ ||18||
(Dayal[das]: at the age of eleven, when the crowning of the kingdom was to take place, Chatursinh reflected: "I shall thereby fall into a trap.")

Dayal[das] — when the prince reached the age of eleven, the royal coronation [rajtilak] began to take place; then Chatursinh thought, "In this way I shall fall back into the snare of maya."

_Dayaala tab manmein chinta bhai, main bhakti kaaj dhari deh; Jo rajko sukh lahu, to kaal pakad mohe leh._ ||19||
(Dayal[das]: then anxiety arose in his mind — "I took this body for the sake of devotion; if I accept the pleasures of kingship, death shall seize me.")

Dayal[das] — [then] anxiety arose in his mind that, "I took this body in order to attain devotion; so if I accept the pleasure of the splendour of the kingdom, then ruin [kaal] will seize me."

_Dayaala — chatur sanghe vichariyo, neekasu aadhi raat; Chalte-chalte tahan jaau, jahan desh Gujarat._ ||20||
(Dayal[das]: Chatursinh reflected, "I shall leave at midnight, and journeying on, go there, to the land of Gujarat.")

Dayal[das] — Chatursinh thought that he would leave at midnight, and travelling on and on, go to where the land of Gujarat is.

_Dayaala Gurjar dharmein aaiya, jahan Sokhado gaam; Chatusinghe vichariyo, ihaan karu visraam._ ||21||
(Dayal[das]: [Jnaniji — Chatursinh] came into the land of Gujarat, to where the village of Sokhda is; Chatusinh thought, "I shall rest here.")

Dayal[das] — Jnaniji [Chatursinh] came to the land of Gujarat, to where the village of Sokhda is, and there Chatusinh thought that he would take rest.

_Dayaala sarovarki paale rahyo, tapsi bhekh samaar; Bhojan denkun nit hi, aave dvijki naar._ ||22||
(Dayal[das]: he stayed on the bank of a lake, wearing the garb of an ascetic; a Brahmin's wife would come every day to bring him food.)

Dayal[das] — wearing the garb of an ascetic [tapasvi], he stayed on the bank of the lake; a Brahmin woman would come every day to give him food.

_Dayaala taakun ek putra tho, maran paamiyo soye; Chatusinghe kripa kari, tabahi sajivan hoy._ ||23||
(Dayal[das]: that woman had one son, who died; Chatusinh showed his grace, and he thereupon came back to life.)

Dayal[das] — that woman had one son, and he died; Chatusinh showed grace, and he then came back to life.

_Dayaala tabahi Chatusinh oothe chale, gaye Sanjhake dwaar; Taahaan Dwarakadasji bhetiya, bohot kari manuhaar._ ||24||
(Dayal[das]: then Chatusinh got up and set out, and came to the gate of Sanjha; there he met Dwarkadasji, who welcomed him with great warmth.)

Dayal[das] — after that, Chatusinh got up from there and set out, and, travelling on, arrived at Sanjha, where he met Dwarkadasji, who received him with great warmth and respect.

_Dayaala Chatusingh charane namya, mohe sunaavo naam; Tab Dwarka dase kripa kari, naam bataayo Ram._ ||25||
(Dayal[das]: Chatusinh bowed at his feet [and said], "Recite the Name to me"; then Dwarkadas, in his grace, gave him the name of Ram.)

Dayal[das] — Chatusinh fell at his feet and said, "Recite God's name for me"; then Dwarkadas graciously gave him the name of Ram, and showed him the devotional practice of remembering [japa of] the name of Ram.

_Dayaala ek same aisi bhai, hase he Dwarakadas; Tab Chatusingh paachhe hasya, tab gure kahyo parkaas._ ||26||
(Dayal[das]: once it so happened that Dwarkadas laughed; then Chatusinh laughed afterward too; then the guru told [him] to reveal [the reason].)

Dayal[das] — once it happened that Dwarkadas began to laugh; then Chatusinh also laughed after him; then the guru asked him to tell the reason why he [the guru] had laughed.

_Dayaala hame hasiya kon khojmein, sohi khoj le aavo; Chatusingh khojan chale, manmein dhari eh bhaavo._ ||27||
(Dayal[das]: "Find out why I laughed and bring that reason to me"; Chatusinh set out to search, holding this thought in his mind.)

Dayal[das] — "Go and find out the reason why I laughed, and bring it [to me]." For this reason, holding this intention in mind, Chatusinh set out to discover the reason.

_Dayaala dhyaan dharyu Revake betmein, mohe male Bhagvan; Sanso mero metke, ohi bataave gnaan._ ||28||
(Dayal[das]: he took up meditation on an island of the Reva [Narmada], thinking, "May God meet me and, dispelling my doubt, reveal the knowledge.")

Dayal[das] — thinking, "If God meets me [there], he will dispel my doubt and reveal the explanation to me," he began meditating on an island of the Narmada [Reva].

_Dayaala saat din tapasya kari, manmein aani dheer; Tab sadguru dayaa kari, jan-ki jaani peer._ ||29||
(Dayal[das]: he practised austerity for seven days, keeping patience in his mind; then the Sadguru, knowing his devotee's suffering, showed grace.)

Dayal[das] — he practised austerities for seven days, keeping patience in his mind; then the Sadguru, knowing the suffering of his devotee, showed grace.

_Dayaala din ugat sadguru mile, daatan keeno aay; Taaki chiran ropke, vatahi kiyo banaay._ ||30||
(Dayal[das]: at daybreak the Sadguru came and met him, having used a tooth-twig; planting the splinters of it, he made [them grow into] a banyan tree.)

Dayal[das] — as the day dawned, Kabirji came and met him, having cleaned his teeth [with a twig]; he then planted the pieces of that twig and made them grow into a banyan tree.

_Dayaala Chatusingh charane namya, chhaandi apno dhyaan; Tum daata ho mugatke, mohe bataavo gnaan._ ||31||
(Dayal[das]: Chatusinh, leaving his meditation, bowed at his feet [and said], "You are the giver of liberation — grant me your knowledge.")

Dayal[das] — leaving his meditation, Chatusinh bowed at his feet and said, "You are the giver of liberation, the deliverer — teach me your knowledge."

_Dayaala tab sadguru-e dayaa kari, bhed bataayo ek; Chatusingh samjhaaiya, kahe jo vaat vivek._ ||32||
(Dayal[das]: then the Sadguru, in his grace, revealed one secret, and explained it to Chatusinh, telling him this discerning matter.)

Dayal[das] — then the Sadguru, in his grace, explained the reason for the doubt to Chatusinh, and told him to tell his guru the secret [of why he had laughed].

_Dayaala tabahi Chatusinh jaayke, guruku sheesh namaay; je sadguru-e samjhaaiya, so guruku kahi samjhaay._ ||33||
(Dayal[das]: then Chatusinh went and, bowing his head to his guru, told and explained to the guru what the Sadguru had explained [to him].)

Dayal[das] — then Chatusinh went to his guru, bowed his head to him, and told and explained to him what the Sadguru had explained to him:

_Dayaala vaari utaarat behe gayo, vatko beej chanik; Tab gurudev yon boliya, vaat kahi ten neek._ ||34||
(Dayal[das]: "While relieving myself, a fig-seed was in an instant swept away — [that is why I laughed]"; then the guru said, "You have spoken the matter well.")

Dayal[das] — [Chatusinh said]: "While I was urinating, the fig-fruit of the banyan tree was swept away in an instant, and seeing that, I laughed." Hearing this, the guru [Dwarkadas] said, "You have told the truth exactly."

_Dayaala tab gurudev yon boliya, ke anbhe upji tohe; Ke sadguru tohe malya, sohi bataavo mohe._ ||35||
(Dayal[das]: then the guru said, "Has fearlessness [true realization] arisen in you? Or has some sadguru met you? Tell me this too.")

Dayal[das] — then the guru went on to say, "Has fearlessness [true realization] now come to you? Or has some such sadguru met you? Tell me that too."

_Dayaala mohe to sadguru malya, sab bhed diya bataay; So tumkun main aaye kahya, mokun sadguru bhaye sahaay._ ||1||
(Dayal[das]: "I did meet a sadguru, who revealed every secret to me; I have come and told you this — the Sadguru became my helper.")

Dayal[das] — [Chatusinh said]: "I did meet a Sadguru [Kabirji], who revealed every secret to me; that is what I have come and told you — thus the Sadguru became my helper."

_Dayaala guru sevak donu gaye, jahan baithe das Kabir; Tab guru-e gnani kahya, sevak bada sudhir._ ||36||
(Dayal[das]: the guru and the disciple both went to where Das Kabir was seated; then the guru called him "Gnani," [saying] "the disciple is of great steadfastness.")

Dayal[das] — the guru [Khojiji — Dwarkadas] and the disciple Chatusinh both went to where Das Kabirji was seated. There the guru addressed Chatusinh by the name "Gnani" and said, "O devotee, you are of great patience and steadfastness."

_Dayaala sadguru saaheb Kabirji, leela agam apaar; Aage bohot vistaar hai, so harde dharo vichaar._ ||38||
(Dayal[das]: the deeds of Sadguru Saheb Kabirji are unfathomable and boundless; there is much more that unfolds further — keep this thought in your heart.)

Dayal[das] — the deeds and character of Sadguru Kabir Saheb are so profound that they cannot be fully fathomed. There is much more of this story yet to come — keep this understanding in your heart.

The prince Chatusinh of the Bhati clan of Jaisalmer, who came to have darshan of Kabirji at Kabirvad [the banyan of Kabir], was gripped by the doubt of whether the seed lies within the tree or the tree within the seed — that doubt in his mind, Kabirji resolved. One who seeks God by roaming through pilgrimage places, temples, and other such shrines of the divine does not find God in this way; likewise, one who merely performs worship, vows, and rituals cannot attain God. Though the Lord Ram pervades all moving and unmoving creation, he is not seen. When Gnaniji, who was searching for that very Ram, had the darshan of Ram in Kabir, Gnaniji asked, "Baba, are you Ram, or are you Kabir?" Kabirji said, "What do you see?" Gnani said, "Outwardly you appear as Kabir, and yet Ram, who dwells within you, appears clearly to me. Why do we not see this in ourselves?" Kabir said, "When can the essence be seen clearly in a vessel of unclean glass? Only when the vessel is clean does the essence appear clear. In the same way, when the mind becomes pure, and your vessel remains clean, the Ram who dwells within you will become visible." It is evident from this episode of Gnaniji, who had the vision of the united form of Ram and Kabir, that —

_Bahar Kabira dekhke, bharam pado jan kaay; Kabir bhitar Ram dhani, Ram Kabir bhinn na hoye. Kabira man nirmal bhaya, Ram hirde raha samaay; Nirmal bartan ras jyu, Kabir antar Ram darshaay._
(Seeing Kabir outwardly, let no devotee fall into delusion; within Kabir dwells the Lord Ram — Ram and Kabir are not separate. Kabir's mind became pure, and Ram came to dwell in his heart; just as the essence shows clear in a clean vessel, so within Kabir, Ram is revealed.)

Let no one — no devotee — fall into delusion upon seeing Kabir outwardly. Within Kabir dwells the Master, Ram; that Ram and Kabir cannot be separate. Kabir's mind became pure, and Ram came to dwell within his heart. Just as the essence appears clear in a clean vessel, so too Ram is clearly seen within Kabir's heart.

Gnaniji, who had this vision of the united form of Ram and Kabir, awakened the Ramkabir tradition. At Kabirvad, he entrusted the seat [gaadi] to Nirdas. There is a memorial inscription at Kabirvad from the time Kabirji came there. Kabirji regarded temples and idols as obstacles to the worship of God and opposed them. Chatusinh, a prince of the Bhatiya clan of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan, was — in a former birth — the yoga-fallen soul Gorakhnath. Since Chatusinh remained detached from worldly life, his royal family arranged his marriage to the princess Pranakunvarba of Jaipur, and the wedding rites were performed; but during the circling [of the sacred fire], upon hearing the word "sāvadhāna" [be alert], he became alert and fled from the wedding rites. He then took initiation from Khojiji, but the matter of the fig-fruit incident remained unresolved; [to resolve it] he went into meditation [samadhi] at Shulpaneshwar and attained mastery of raja-yoga, but even so his doubt was not resolved. Then he came to Kabirji at Kabirvad, who had given Tattvajiva true recognition of a true saint, and he attained discipleship. Gnaniji's bodyguard and Pranakunvarba too came to Kabirvad. Kabirji explained to Gnaniji that devotion to Hari can be practised even while remaining in householder life; non-attachment is more important than renunciation. Remaining unattached, and through understanding of the mind, one can attain God even while living in the world. Through loving devotion, rather than through renunciation, God can be attained more readily. Gnaniji spent his householder life with Pranakunvar in the great village of Sanja. A religious assembly was held at this place, in which the pandit Sarvajit, defeated in debate, became a disciple of Kabirji.

Anantdas has said, in Kabir's Parachai [hagiography]:

_Ramkabir ekhimeka, jin koi karo apni teka; Jan te thakor te jan hoi, aisi jugat bani hai doi. Pala re jal ten upajya, funi pala jal maanhi samaaya; Bhakt bhagvant aadya hai doi, jhoothe bharam pado mat koi._ ||9-10||
(Ram and Kabir are one and the same — let none rely on doubt regarding them; the devotee becomes the Lord, and the Lord becomes the devotee — such is the way the two are joined. Frost arises from water, and again dissolves back into water; the devotee and God have both existed from the beginning — let none fall into false delusion.)

Ram and Kabir are interwoven with each other, so, by mistake, let no one harbour any doubt about them. The devotee — the Harijan — is God himself, and God is the Harijan himself; such is the mystery contained within these two. Ice is born from water and again dissolves back into water; in the same way, the devotee — the Harijan — and God are, from time immemorial, inseparable from each other. So do not fall into any false delusion.

Brahmalin Muni writes: history says that Gnani had the direct darshan of Guru Kabir Saheb. By Kabirji's grace he had the darshan of Ram; therefore he united Ram and Kabir and uttered the word "Ramkabir."
